utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-02-58-I, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Ljubisa Beara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who appears for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Peter McCloskey, and today with me are Lise-Lotte Karlsson and Salvador Viada.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Gregor Guy-Smith and I am appearing on behalf of Mr. Beara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. Now, your client has received a copy of this indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He has, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And it contains six charges of which he is fully aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is it your intention to tender any plea today in relation to any of these charges?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It follows, therefore, that arrangements will require to be made for an occasion when plea can be tendered within the next 30 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: One would hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you give me some indication of when you're likely to be in a position to tender a plea?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe that we may be in a position to tender a plea somewhere within the next two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: One possibility is simply to continue this initial appearance for as near the maximum period as possible to avoid any difficulty, so say four weeks, or would you rather it was continued until an earlier date than that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe that if we could continue it for the latter period of time, meaning closer to four weeks, that would be preferable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. McCloskey, if that is the arrangement and the case is appointed to call again on the 9th of November, that would be four weeks from today, at the same time in the day, would that cause any difficulty for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The only thing that I would request is that when Mr. Beara has decided finally and firmly on his legal counsel, that we be informed, because we do have the confirmation materials, though I've found that it's best to provide them to the actual lawyer that is going to take the case, because otherwise they tend to get, sometimes, caught in betwixt and between.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, can you help at all on that question when that's likely to be clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I can't at this moment. I wish that I could, which is part of the reason I'm asking for as much time as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Beara, you've heard all that's been exchanged between myself and counsel, I take it. And I take it you understand that the case will be called again in the Tribunal on the 9th of November. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On that occasion, you will be required, in terms of the Rules, to tender a plea of guilty or not guilty to the various charges against you. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit again. Now, does either counsel wish to raise any other matter with me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: None at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. I shall appoint the case to call again --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated] I wished to ask His Honour whether I can put another question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is your question, Mr. Beara?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not really a question, Your Honour. I wish to say something. All of those who will see this or hear this or whatever, my comrades at arms who are now accused and who are fugitives, I wish to send a message to them that they voluntarily surrender as soon as possible to get the stone that is around the neck of our nation off our country. That is what I wish to say to all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Beara.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The case will be called again on the 9th of November, on which occasion, Mr. Beara, you will be expected to tender your plea. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: at 3.12 p.m.
